intro: Popovers open from a trigger and hold interactive content such as short forms, status details, and compact action panels. Use them when a tooltip is too passive and a modal is too heavy.
useCases: Open quick-edit forms from dense tables.
Show notification summaries without leaving the current page.
Collect a small amount of metadata near the related control.
Expose secondary actions while preserving the current workflow.

faqs.question: When should I use Popover instead of Tooltip?
faqs.answer: Use Tooltip for short, non-interactive hints. Use Popover when the content needs focusable controls, links, forms, or click-driven disclosure.

faqs.question: Does the Popover component work with Next.js App Router?
faqs.answer: Yes. Popover is a client component because it manages open state, outside clicks, and keyboard dismissal. Import it inside client boundaries where the trigger is interactive.

faqs.question: Can I theme Popover with CSS variables?
faqs.answer: Yes. Popover follows the Zentauri UI token pattern with --zui-popover-* variables for content surfaces, brand appearances, and gradients.

sections.heading: What it does
sections.body:
Popover provides click-triggered floating content that can contain buttons, inputs, links, and compact workflows.

It closes on outside click and Escape by default, while supporting controlled state for application-managed overlays.

sections.heading: Composition and API
sections.body: Use Popover, PopoverTrigger, and PopoverContent as compound parts. Content controls side, align, width, size, and variant independently from the trigger.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.body: The trigger exposes expanded state and controls the dialog content. Keep labels visible, preserve focus rings, and test keyboard-only flows when content contains form controls.

sections.heading: Next.js integration notes
sections.body: Keep Popover usage in client components. Static page copy and SEO can remain server-rendered, while the interactive preview islands import the popover primitives.
